content.one_sentence_role: Names the intersection of two closed balls with a common radius.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $E$ be a normed additive commutative group, let $x,y\in E$, and let $r\in\mathbb R$. The symmetric lens with foci $x,y$ and radius $r$ is the set $\Lambda_r(x,y)$ defined below.
content.definition_explanation: Write $\overline B(x,r)=\{z\in E:\|z-x\|\le r\}$. Then $$\Lambda_r(x,y)=\overline B(x,r)\cap\overline B(y,r)=\{z\in E:\|z-x\|\le r\ \text{and}\ \|z-y\|\le r\}.$$ Thus membership imposes both closed distance bounds with the same radius.
content.assumptions: Only the normed additive commutative group $E$, two points $x,y$, and a real number $r$ are required. The foci may coincide, and $r$ need not be positive.
content.conclusion: The output is a subset of $E$, symmetric in its two foci: $\Lambda_r(x,y)=\Lambda_r(y,x)$. If $r<0$, it is empty because norms are nonnegative. No midpoint or reflection assertion is part of this definition.
